text: {"findings":[{"rule_id":"MF-005","evidence":[{"kind":"title_block","ref":"heat_treatment","page":1,"quote":"TO BE TOUGHENED UPTO 24-32 HRC."}],"comment":"The heat treatment is specified but the drawing does not state at which manufacturing stage it applies (e.g., before or after final machining), which matters because hardening to 24-32 HRC affects machinability and dimensional stability. The designer should add a note clarifying when the toughening is to be performed relative to machining operations.","recommended_correction":"Add a note specifying the stage, for example 'HEAT TREAT AFTER ROUGH MACHINING, BEFORE FINISH MACHINING' or similar process sequence."},{"rule_id":"ISO-012","evidence":[{"kind":"dimension","ref":"D21","page":1,"quote":"20±0.02"},{"kind":"dimension","ref":"D19","page":1,"quote":"62±0.1"},{"kind":"dimension","ref":"D22","page":1,"quote":"50±0.1"}],"comment":"Dimension D21 (20±0.02) appears to define the distance between the two ⌀8 H7 locating holes (F1), yet it is not dimensioned directly between the hole centers; instead it seems derived from other dimensions such as D19 and D22, leaving this tight functional distance dependent on accumulated tolerances. Functional distances between mating features must be dimensioned directly so the tolerance band is not consumed by stack-up. The designer should add a direct center-to-center dimension between the two H7 holes with the ±0.02 tolerance.","recommended_correction":"Replace the indirect dimensioning scheme with a single direct dimension between the two ⌀8 H7 hole centers carrying the 20±0.02 tolerance."}]}
